Inside Kairo

The booking, payment and customer-messaging system a service business runs its whole day on — photographed screen by screen, in the order a visitor should meet it.

I

The owner opens the app

What do I need to know right now?

  • Today at a glanceBooked, done, still to come, taken against expected, and how much of the day is still free.
  • With you now / Next upWho is in the chair and who is next, re-derived from the clock every 30 seconds.
  • The run of the dayPast visits recede, the current one is marked, and the free gaps are called out.
  • Client notes on the dayAllergies, colour formulas and preferences surface on the appointment itself.
  • Growth and retentionNew vs returning, a rebooking rate, and a win-back list of regulars who have drifted.
  • Rhythm and trendsWhich hours are busiest, revenue per day, and the top-selling services.
II

The day book

The diary, but it cannot be double-booked.

  • A column per team memberColour-coded, blocks sized to the real length of each service.
  • Drag to rescheduleMove a booking to a new time or a different stylist; drag its edge to make it longer.
  • Multi-service bookingsColour + blow dry is one appointment with the combined time and price.
  • Block out timeLunch, training, a delivery, a day off — with a private reason only the owner sees.
  • Booked-online markerEvery appointment shows whether it came from the public page or the salon.
III

Changes that do not cost you a customer

The part competitors get wrong.

  • Every booking and move asks who to tellEmail them, text them, both, or nothing — only channels that client can actually receive.
  • A move leads with the old timeSo a client skimming it sees a change, not a duplicate confirmation they will ignore.
  • Undo a cancellationThe message is held two minutes; tap Undo and the booking returns exactly as it was.
  • It refuses to lieIf the slot was retaken it will not double-book; if the message went out, it says so.
IV

The client book

Everything you know about them, wherever you are.

  • A profile per clientUpcoming visits, full history, invoices, lifetime spend, notes.
  • Notes that follow the clientAnything typed on a booking is copied to their record, dated, for next time.
  • Import from a spreadsheetReads real Excel files, matches on email then phone then name, never duplicates.
  • Merge duplicatesFinds clients sharing an email, phone or name and merges the whole history across.
V

Getting paid

From the chair to the bank without a second app.

  • Point of saleBill one of today’s appointments or a walk-in: services, retail, custom lines, discounts.
  • Card, cash, transfer or StripeIncluding a pay-link the customer opens on their own phone.
  • Invoices and receiptsDraft, sent and paid, tax handled, receipts sent the moment payment lands.
  • Retail and stockMargins, stock levels, and a warning before the shelf is empty.
  • DepositsTake a percentage up front online, credited automatically at checkout.
VI

Talking to customers, automatically

The single biggest no-show reducer.

  • Confirmations and remindersSent on booking, and a set number of hours before the visit.
  • Email, SMS, or bothChosen per message type — or per booking, at the moment of saving.
  • Review requestsSent automatically after a visit, with a reviews page and the ability to reply.
  • A complete logEvery message, its channel and its status. Nothing sends or fails silently.
VII

What the customer sees

The shopfront that never closes.

  • A booking page on your own linkBranded to the business, and it updates itself when prices or hours change.
  • Only real openings are offeredComputed from bookings, blocked time and hours — then re-checked at the moment of confirming.
  • Terms before they commitThe cancellation notice is stated on the page, not buried in an email.
  • A cancel link in every messageThe client can cancel up to the notice period; the slot reopens instantly.
VIII

Set up once, then forget it

  • Guided setup on first runThe business, its hours, its team, its services.
  • Hours that match realityPer-day hours, and days that run only every 2nd, 3rd or 4th week.
  • Booking window and noticeHow far ahead customers can book, and the deadline for cancelling online.
  • The team and the menuColours, titles, individual hours; categories, durations and three price types.
IX

In the hand

The whole salon in an apron pocket.

  • The same workspace on a phoneInstalls to the home screen. No app store, no download, no second version.
  • Pull down to refreshThe gesture every phone app has trained people to expect.
X

Built differently

For the reader who asks how it is made.

  • Zero dependenciesNo frameworks, no packages, no build step. Nothing breaks when a library updates.
  • One file per businessThe whole business lives in a single database file that can be copied or moved in one move.
  • Security taken seriouslyParameterised queries, signed HttpOnly sessions, server-side authorisation, rate limiting, password breach checks.
  • Honest about its own stateIt detects a wrong time zone, a disk that will be wiped, and a default password still in use — and says so.
